opportunities.title: Coldcard Got Hacked. $15B in Bitcoin Just Proved Nobody Trusts 'Cold' Anymore
opportunities.why_now: A hardware wallet compromise triggered a mass flight of $15B in BTC within days, and investigators are now publicly tracing the stolen funds — a rare real-time forensics story.
opportunities.angle: Explainer/postmortem: walk through how the tracing works, then pivot to the uncomfortable truth that 'cold storage' is a process, not a device — end with a checklist of what actually changes after this.

opportunities.title: Harmony Wants to Roll Back the Chain Again. We've Seen This Movie.
opportunities.why_now: Harmony is openly weighing a rollback after a suspected exploit inflated ONE supply — the same 'immutability is optional when it's inconvenient' playbook crypto has run before.
opportunities.angle: Sharp opinion piece: use the rollback discussion as the hook to revisit every prior 'temporary' rollback in crypto history and what it actually signals to sophisticated attackers about which chains are soft targets.

opportunities.title: Coinsbuy's $100K Bounty Is a Confession, Not a Solution
opportunities.why_now: Coinsbuy just offered a $100K reward days after a Sunday breach reportedly drained $7.9M in wallets — the classic post-hack negotiation-via-bounty move.
opportunities.angle: Pattern piece: catalog how the 'reward for return' playbook has performed historically (recovery rates, negotiation outcomes) and what it really tells depositors about the exchange's actual security posture before the hack.

opportunities.title: The XRP Bridge Didn't Get Hacked — It Just Believed What It Was Told
opportunities.why_now: A bridge was drained because its software treated fake deposits as real, a textbook trust-boundary failure rather than a sophisticated exploit.
opportunities.angle: Technical teardown for a security-literate audience: explain the specific validation gap, then generalize into 'every bridge is a trust assumption wearing a UI' — the recurring failure mode this channel is known for calling out.

opportunities.title: Bitcoin Firms Are Asking AI Labs for the Same Tools Attackers Already Have
opportunities.why_now: Crypto companies are publicly lobbying AI firms for early access to frontier models to help Bitcoin developers — an admission that offense is already ahead of defense.
opportunities.angle: Analysis piece connecting this to the same-week 'Zoomsday' story (a critical exploit built by AI in one day): argue the asymmetry is now structural, not hypothetical, and lay out what defenders should actually do while they wait for access they may never get.
